results.title: Call for papers Decolonizing Marketing Theory and Practice – going beyond the inclusivity and sustainability debates by Dr Hasan Gilani There is a lot of discussion and arguments around the subject of decolonising the syllabus, curriculum and even the entire university experiences at academic institutions. It is becoming increasingly clear and important that there should be conversations that should go deeper than the apparent blogs, hashtags and social media hit counts. Extending the works of Banerji (2021), Eckhardt et al, (2021) and Dar et al., (2021), this book would explore the different avenues to decolonize Marketing theory and practice. The focus of the discussions would be to go beyond the basics of adding authors of non-white ethnicity or adding some examples from the non-Western countries. Decolonising the curriculum is not just about adding literature and case studies from non-Western countries, but it is about challenging the roots of colonisation which is capitalism and inequality. Decolonisation should have starting points at inclusivity and equality as prime focus, and then move towards recognition and exploration of contexts and paradigms. The main aim of the book would be to look at the epistemological and ontological shifts of paradigm in the marketing subject area. With the recent advents of post pandemic regional conflicts, wars, movement of immigrants across the world, and the on-going issues of unemployment, poor educational outcomes, and the mainstream education being only limited to the developed Western world, there is a dire need to understand multiculturalism, not only in the context of teaching and disseminating knowledge, but also diversity in learning experiences of the learners. World’s top business schools and top academic journals belong to the white dominated Western world, where every theory, every research ontology is viewed with a white privileged lens by the white dominant academics who decide what is a good level of research and what isn’t. The proposed book would attempt to challenge this dominance and incorporate views from the non-Western world on the subject area. Adapted from the concept of circular economy, circular pedagogy focuses on continuous process of learning and teaching processes through the interactions between the learners, the facilitators (teachers) and research activities. However, there is a strong presence of (inclusive and diverse) curriculum and content of knowledge that acts as a catalyst in this process which ensures collaborative continuity and sustainability of learning and teaching experiences. This book would explore the idea of adopting a circular pedagogical approach to Marketing discipline to make it more sustainable and inclusive at the same time. Keywords Decolonisation, Marketing, Marketing Theory, Inclusive Marketing, Paradigm shift, Decolonising the curriculum. Statement of Aims The book would contribute on the subject area of decolonising the marketing syllabus and make it more inclusive. The book would explore different avenues of pedagogical development in context of marketing theory and practice and identify areas where text, knowledge and contexts need to be decolonised and a shift of paradigm from culture of exclusion and western ideologies towards being open to inclusivity and a wide range of philosophical stance from the non-western world. This book aims to encourage rethinking of curriculum design, particularly in the Marketing discipline, and making the mainstream curricula more inclusive learning environments through the use of technological advances. The book would challenge the current literature and methodological approaches towards Marketing theory and practice and incorporate a more circular pedagogical view towards sustainable education. The following are a few key aims of the book: -To identify the different approaches towards decolonising the Marketing theory and practice core texts with more inclusive curricula incorporated multicultural and diverse set of knowledge, theories, debates and case studies. -To challenge the current colonial rooted knowledge and debates within the Marketing discipline and invite more discussions from the non-western world within the realm of Marketing theory and practices. -To identify ways of making the discipline sustainable by adopting circular pedagogical approaches of continues learning and evolving of knowledge and learning experiences. Table of Contents Proposed Table of Contents Following is a proposed set of chapters which are subject to change due to the preferences of the authors. However, the essence of the sections would more-or-less remain the same within the set parameters. Section A: Decolonising Marketing theory and practice - a paradigm shift This section would focus on discussions on decolonising the marketing discipline and how to ensure the inclusivity and diversity within the discipline is not just at a superficial level where they add new material from the non-Western world into existing theory and body of knowledge, but it should focus on new paradigms and knowledge emerging from the non-Western societies as well. With the majority of top business schools located in the Western world, the knowledge and theories emerging would be West focused covering issues relating to the Western world. This chapter would expand the canvas and represent issues, knowledge, theories and context emerging from the non-Western academia. The section would also focus on how Marketing Research, methodologies and scales should be decolonised and made more inclusive. Chapter 1: A New Educational Paradigm to Decolonise Marketing Practice Authors: Hasan Gilani (The University of Brighton), Lucía Morales (Technological University Dublin), Nadia Barkoczi (Technical University of Cluj-Napoca), Lia Pop (Technical University of Cluj- Napoca), Patrick Flynn (Technological University Dublin) Chapter 2: The notion of market and its Western vs Indigenous meanings - a public-private distinction (Prof Nimruji Jammulamadaka, IIM Calcutta, India) Chapter 3: Decolonizing Marketing. Consumption, Markets, and Culture (Prof Susan Dobscha, Bentley University, USA) Chapter 4: Technology and Innovation to Decolonise Marketing Research Methods Authors: Authors: Daniel Rajmil (Universitat Oberta de Catalunya), Claudia Marian (Technical University of Cluj-Napoca), Iulia Stepan (Technical University of Cluj-Napoca) , Georgia Savvidou (Cyprus Technological University) Chapter 5: Diversity and inclusivity in marketing research epistemology and ontology Section B: Going beyond the Inclusivity and Diversity debates in Marketing theory and practice This section would cover topics relating to nurturing and identifying multiculturalism in the marketing discipline and how it should be fostered throughout the learning and research process within the subject area. Most of the contemporary literature in marketing and other business modules, is focused on climate change and sustainability, whereas there are more serious issues facing the Middle Eastern, African and East Asian countries. Climate change is 13th on the list of 17 UN SDGs. The issues of poverty, education, slavery, and healthcare have been completely missing from the marketing syllabus and needs to be incorporated in theoretical debates. By expanding the debates beyond the obvious climate change and sustainability (which are extremely important ofcourse), the book would be incorporating views on marketing from different cultures across the world. This would give more wider scope to sub-topics such as halal branding, dark tourism (destination branding), inclusive advertising and inclusive social media marketing research. Chapter 5: Inclusive Marketing – going beyond the CSR and climate debates. (Dr Charo Chalezquer and Prof Arrese, University of Navarra) Chapter 6: Inclusivity and Diversity: Marketing Exercise or a Real Commitment? Authors: Lia Pop (Technical University Cluj-Napoca), María Victoria Soulé (Cyprus Technological University), Ivaylo Peev (Technical University Sofia), Todor Todorov (Technical University Sofia), Hasan Gilani (University of Brighton) Chapter 7: Inclusive Marketing debates – challenging the western centric focus and widening the scope Chapter 8: Creating a team culture that fosters inclusive marketing (Becky Stenlund and Katie Jensen, University of St. Thomas) Section C: Towards a sustainable pedagogical approach This section would primarily focus on a sustainable approach to the learning and teaching experiences and ensure continuous improvement in the pedagogical development process of the discipline. Extending the recent works of Pop et al, (2022) and Morales et al. (2022), this section would focus on a sustainable approach towards pedagogical developments in the subject area of Marketing theory and practices. Applying the concepts of circular pedagogy and incorporating inclusivity and diversity in the teaching, research and learning experiences of the discipline, this section would pave way for future research and thought-provoking prospects on the topics. Chapter 9: Circular Pedagogy – towards a sustainable yet inclusive education model Authors: Lucía Morales (Technological University Dublin), Yann Verchier (University of Technology of Troyes), Jon-Hans Coetzer (United Nations Institute for Training and Research), Elis Constantinou (Cyprus Technological University), Nadia Barkoczi (Technical University Cluj-Napoca), Hasan Gilani (University of Brighton) Chapter 10: Facilitators, Constraints and Trepidations in Decolonising Transnational Education – towards a more inclusive approach (Dr Ron Cambridge, London Metropolitan University) Chapter 11: Transdisciplinary Education for Smart Sustainable Development (Dr Lucia Morales) Chapter 12: Decolonizing Marketing Education through Circular Pedagogy: Teaching Inclusive Multicultural Marketing through Digital Service-Learning focused on Marginalized Businesswomen (Dr Rivera Reynaldo, Universidad Austral, Argentina) Length and schedule There would be three sections in the book, each section would have 4-5 chapters. Each chapter would have around 6-7000 words, and a total of 12-14 chapters for the entire book. Once the proposal is approved, I would then approach potential collaborators to agree on the content, direction and scope of the chapters, alongwith a realistic timeline. I aim to complete the chapters within 7-8 months of the time of proposal approval, including summer period where academic have most of the time to write-up. Please contact email h.gilani@brighton.ac.uk to discuss your potential chapter for contribution. Send your proposed chapter summary by 15th March 2023. results.content: # ICA Public Relations Division | Hi to all of you interested in regional perspectives in PR and strategic communication (and maybe even the Nordic region) | Facebook. ## ICA Public Relations Division ·. Hi to all of you interested in regional perspectives in PR and strategic communication (and maybe even the Nordic region). We recently hosted a paper development workshop at BI Norwegian Business School to share and work on research focusing on Nordic perspectives in strategic communication. On 28 February 2025 is the deadline for submitting manuscripts for the special issue on this theme in the International Journal of Strategic Communication. For all interested, here is the CfP: https://think.taylorandfrancis.com/.../nordic.../. Nice to see Dr Øyvind Ihlen, excellent scholar on PR and Organisational communication.

results.content: ## Journal of Management Studies's Post. ### **Journal of Management Studies**. 🚨 Call for Papers: JMS & SAMS 2026 Conference 🚨. 📝 Submit by: 5 December 2025. Truth in the Age of Polarization and Artificial Intelligence. As AI-generated content proliferates, organizations strategically shape knowledge, and polarization erodes common ground, the very concept of "truth" is being questioned, negotiated, and weaponized in ways that profoundly affect society, organizations, and our collective future. At the 2026 Journal of Management Studies Conference, we seek contributions that explore:. ✅ How truth is constructed and contested in organizations and society. ✅ The impact of AI on truth, trust, and organizational legitimacy. ✅ The role of identity, power, and narrative in shaping what we consider "true". Selected proposals will be presented and discussed at the conference to advance collective thinking. • Proposal submission: 5 December 2025. Join us in Cambridge to co-create a more nuanced, inclusive, and critical understanding of truth in our field and beyond.
